This manual contains the instructions and course material for the 4 of the 8 sessions in **4.3 Programming Experiments**. These four-sessions will be a hands-on introduction to building online behavioural experiments with [jsPsych](https://www.jspsych.org), complementing the sessions on programming experiments with E-Prime.

JsPsych is open-source software, which means you can follow this tutorial and complete the exercises on your own computer. You can also work on the lab computers.

By the end of the course, you will have built and hosted a complete, real experiment of your own choosing, from a blank file to a public URL that collects real data.

## Schedule

| Session | Title | Topic |
|------------------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | [Foundations](sessions/session1.qmd) | HTML, CSS, JavaScript basics, and your first jsPsych experiment |
| 2 | [Trial Design](sessions/session2.qmd) | Multiple trial types, randomization, feedback, practice and main blocks |
| 3 | [Real Data](sessions/session3.qmd) | Timeline variables, consent, participant data, saving and inspecting results |
| 4 | [Going Live](sessions/session4.qmd) | Building a complete experiment from a specification, and hosting it online |

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, you will be able to:

- **Operationalize an experiment**: turn a research question or classic paradigm into a concrete, working set of trials.
- Present stimuli in different modalities such as **text,** and **images**
- Control and reason about **trial timing**: fixation crosses, stimulus duration, and response windows.
- Collect different types of response: **key presses, reaction times, and choices** (including button-based responses).
- **Randomize** trial order and materials, and (optionally) **counterbalance** condition order across participants.
- Implement **performance feedback**, and (optionally) simple **adaptive logic** that responds to how a participant is doing.
- **Collect, save, and prepare data for analysis**, including opening it cleanly in Excel or SPSS.

## Learning Activities

### Self-study

Each session builds directly on the last with the same running example (and, from Session 4, your own chosen experiment) carrying on through the whole course. Working through each session's exercises yourself, in order, matters more than reading ahead.

### In-session work

Each session is a hands-on, roughly 3-hour block combining short explanations with guided "try it yourself" exercises, working directly in your own project files. Reference solutions ("checkpoint" files) are provided throughout, so you can check your own work or catch up if you fall behind.

::: callout-note
## Before Session 1

You'll need [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/) installed, with the **Live Server** extension. See Session 1's "Before the Practical" section for full setup instructions.
:::


## Getting the Materials

Each session's starter files, images, and library files are available as downloadable templates, see [Templates & Materials](materials.qmd).
